title: Load a tube furnace for two-precursor thermal CVD and cap the tube
instruction: Load the boats for CVD: yellow precursor 1 just inside the furnace's upstream end, white precursor 2 under the thermocouple, the substrate 50 to 80 mm downstream of it; rack the rod and cap the tube.
context: In two-precursor thermal CVD (as for 2D semiconductors), each precursor sits at its own temperature along the furnace and the substrate just downstream of the hotter one; it takes pushing boats blind along a tube with a rod, and sealing both ends.
setup: A split-tube furnace, 370 x 280 mm, lid open, on the bench, with a thermocouple tip at its chamber's centre. In it a fixed fused-quartz tube, 50.8 mm OD, 46 mm ID, 610 mm long, both end caps off; argon comes in at the near end (upstream): each lies in a cradle beside its end, its open end towards the tube's line (the argon inlet's cap beyond the boat tray, away from the robots; the exhaust's cap at the far end, nearer the robots). Each cap is a stainless cup, 66 mm OD, 58 mm bore (a loose fit on the tube) and 18 mm deep, its mouth chamfered from 64 to 58 mm across, 0.1 kg, with a flat tab 28 x 22 x 5 mm standing out of the middle of its end, on its axis, to hold it by (brass on the inlet's cap, black on the exhaust's). Beside the near end, a stainless tray holds three loose boats side by side, each with a 5 mm square tongue at its back: an alumina boat 60 x 20 x 12 mm with 4 mm of yellow powder (precursor 1), 12 g; an alumina boat 60 x 20 x 12 mm with 4 mm of white powder (precursor 2), 12 g; a quartz boat 35 x 20 x 12 mm, 6 g, holding a 10 x 10 x 0.5 mm silicon substrate, its oxidised face up (purple). On a rack of two V rests beside the tube's line, nearer the robots, lies a fused-quartz push rod: a tube 8 mm OD and 218 mm long, 15 g, with a flat paddle on its front, 4 mm thick, 11.5 mm tall with its foot bevelled, and 14 to 20 mm wide, and a flat block 38 x 32 x 5 mm on its back end to hold it by.
scoring: 0 if any boat tips over 20 degrees or drops 30 mm, or the substrate tilts over 30 degrees or its centre leaves the inside of its boat, at any time; 0 unless the boats, substrate, rod and caps moved under 1 mm in the last second. Otherwise 0.2 for each boat in the tube on its floor and in place: precursor 1 centred within 15 mm of 10 mm inside the furnace's near (upstream) end; precursor 2 centred within 10 mm of the thermocouple; the substrate's boat's centre 50 to 80 mm downstream of precursor 2's. And 0.1 for each cap seated on its end of the tube: its end plate within 5 mm of the tube's end, its axis within 5 mm of the tube's and 8 degrees of square. 1.0 if all three boats and both caps, the rod back on its rack (within 15 mm of its start) and every fingertip 8 cm or more from the rod, the boats and the caps.
reset_notes: Put the boats back on the tray, the rod on its rack and the caps in their cradles; the powders and the substrate are reused.
fidelity: Rigid-body sim. Furnace, tube, tray, rack and cradles are fixed; boats, substrate, rod and caps are loose with real sizes and masses, except the substrate at 0.4 g (4x real). Powder is a solid layer, so spills are scored by tilt. No heat, gas or growth: the layout is scored from positions. Caps slip on (no O-ring); gas hoses not modelled. Quartz renders opaque: a boat in the tube shows only by the rod's depth.
